143.title: Differentials — poor feeding neonate
143.subtitle: Near-miss diagnoses to process before you close the case.

items.label: Duodenal obstruction / malrotation
items.why: Vomiting after feeds — but classically **bilious** emesis and surgical abdomen. Timing overlaps, yet you will not see elevated galactose or deficient **GALT** on RBCs.
items.discriminator: Obstruction = mechanical blockage after feeds. Galactosemia = **milk sugar toxin** → jaundice, hepatomegaly, cataracts, sepsis risk.

items.label: E. coli sepsis (galactosemic infants)
items.why: Galactosemic neonates are at **increased sepsis risk** — fever, tachycardia, lethargy overlap. Blood cultures may still be sent, but the **newborn screen / galactose level** and **GALT assay** anchor the metabolic diagnosis.
items.discriminator: Treat infection if present — but do not miss stopping **galactose** while you work up sepsis.

items.label: Biliary atresia / obstructive cholestasis
items.why: Conjugated hyperbilirubin and acholic stools — persistent jaundice beyond the first weeks. This infant's crisis tracks **milk feeds** and metabolic toxin, not isolated bile duct obliteration.
items.discriminator: Feed-locked symptoms + elevated galactose → metabolic, not primary surgical biliary disease.

items.label: Hypoglycemia from blocked gluconeogenesis
items.why: Not a separate diagnosis — it is a **consequence** of GALT blockade. Hepatocytes cannot route galactose into glycolysis → **ATP crash** → lethargy, poor feeding, seizures.
items.discriminator: Check glucose, but the fix is still **eliminate galactose** and confirm **GALT** deficiency.

035.title: Differentials — alcohol withdrawal
035.subtitle: Autonomic storm + AMS after last drink — what else can kill before DTs?

items.label: Alcohol withdrawal / delirium tremens
items.why: Chronic GABA ↑ + NMDA ↓ with abrupt cessation → **rebound glutamate hyperexcitability**. Timeline 24–72 h, tremor, diaphoresis, hallucinations, seizures. **CIWA** guides benzo dosing.
items.discriminator: Last-drink history + autonomic hyperactivity + tremor — treat with benzos even while you rule out mimics.

items.label: Intracranial hemorrhage / traumatic brain injury
items.why: New seizure + AMS in a patient who falls when intoxicated. Check for focal deficits, battle sign, coagulopathy from liver disease.
items.discriminator: CT head if trauma, coagulopathy, focal neuro, or incomplete recovery between events.

items.label: Meningitis / encephalitis
items.why: Fever, AMS, headache overlap. Immunocompromise and nuchal rigidity push this up.
items.discriminator: LP after imaging if suspicion — do not let benzos mask the need for cultures.

items.label: Hypoglycemia, hyponatremia, hepatic encephalopathy
items.why: Fingerstick glucose first. Cirrhosis → **hypoglycemia**, low Na⁺, ammonia ↑ with asterixis.
items.discriminator: **Thiamine before glucose** (Wernicke). Correct Na⁺ slowly; check ammonia if cirrhosis.

items.label: Sympathomimetic / other substance toxidrome
items.why: Cocaine, amphetamines, PCP — tachycardia, hypertension, agitation mimic withdrawal.
items.discriminator: Urine tox screen + history; benzos still help agitation but stimulant MI/ischemia needs its own workup.

items.label: Upper GI bleed (varices)
items.why: Chronic alcohol → portal HTN. Tachycardia, hypotension, melena — shock can present with AMS.
items.discriminator: Hemoglobin trend, rectal exam, type & screen — resuscitate while treating withdrawal.

items.label: Alcohol withdrawal / delirium tremens
items.why: Tom's timeline fits **rebound glutamate hyperexcitability** after abrupt cessation. Prior DT raises risk for seizures and autonomic collapse. **CIWA-Ar** drives symptom-triggered benzos until sedated but arousable.
items.discriminator: Autonomic surge and altered sensorium after reduced drinking — correlate timing with last use.

items.label: Sedative / benzo overdose overlap
items.why: Uber thread: chronic users may take **benzos or sedatives** with alcohol. Overlap can blunt withdrawal signs then unmask with clearance — or present as mixed toxidrome.
items.discriminator: Overlap with sedatives can blur the picture — review meds and tox screen.

items.label: Intracranial hemorrhage / fall trauma
items.why: Tom may fall when intoxicated or seizing. New AMS + seizure → scan if focal deficits, anticoagulation, or incomplete recovery.
items.discriminator: Trauma history or focal neuro signs — imaging when the exam supports it.

items.label: Wernicke encephalopathy
items.why: Chronic alcohol → **thiamine depletion**. Confusion, ataxia, ophthalmoplegia — often incomplete triad.
items.discriminator: Ataxia or eye-movement findings — nutritional history matters.

items.label: Hypoglycemia · hyponatremia · hepatic encephalopathy
items.why: Fingerstick first. Cirrhosis → hypoglycemia, low Na⁺, ammonia ↑ with asterixis.
items.discriminator: Check glucose and basic chemistries early.

items.label: Upper GI bleed (varices)
items.why: Portal HTN from chronic alcohol — tachycardia and hypotension can look like withdrawal autonomics.
items.discriminator: Hemodynamic instability with GI history — look for bleeding stigmata.
